_doc: Named calibration settings per voice, for the audition page. A key is a voice slug — the same string `make_audition.py` names its output directory, the set picker shows and a render's address carries — so `tools/voicematch/bank.py` is what says which keys are legal, and `test_calibration.py` fails on one that matches no voice. Each entry lists settings in the order they should appear on the page, after the unmodified build and before anything `--variant` adds on the command line. Read only when a run passes `--calibrations`: every setting is one more render of every take, and the override layer needs a -DBUILD_TUNING=ON library, so a page opened to hear one voice should not pay for it.
_overrides: The value of SONARE_TUNING_OVERRIDES, passed to the library untouched — the library is the only thing that can say whether a key exists. Keys are scoped: an engine constant is `<file stem>.<name>` (`brass_voice.kLipCouple`), a patch field is `<patch>.<path>` (`trumpet.brass.brassiness`), and a drum note's patch is `d038.percussion.wire_buzz`. A bare constant name resolves when it is unique across the tree and not otherwise — four voices declare `kBreathBase`. `autofit.py --out result.json` writes a paste-ready string, which is where most of these come from.
_copies: A patch prefix reaches THAT patch and no other, which is not where a source edit stops. `overdriven` and `distortion` are built by copying `electric_guitar` as the fallback tables are built, and the copy is taken from the compiled-in values before each patch is tuned under its own name — so editing the source propagates to all three and `electric_guitar.ks.brightness=…` moves programs 26 and 27 alone. The failure is silent and it renders: the program the setting was aimed at comes back byte-identical to the unmodified build, which reads as a knob with no effect rather than as a key that arrived somewhere else. A candidate meant for a copy needs its own entry under that copy's own voice.
_note: What the setting is for, in one line, shown on the page under the version button. It is the only place a candidate says why it is a candidate: the override string says what moved and never says what it was trying to fix, and a page is read weeks after it was built.
_name: The source key: letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`. It is the button label, the file stem and the last segment of the address, so what is on the button, what is in the URL and what is in a listening note are one string. `model` is taken by the unmodified build.
_open: A setting listed here is a candidate that has NOT been written back to the source. That is what the file is for: an override string kept only in a render directory under the scratch root is lost with the directory, and one harpsichord round's candidates were lost exactly that way. Recording is not adoption — a setting stays here until it is either written back (and deleted from here in the same change) or judged and deleted.

variants.name: softer-plectrum
variants.note: the reference is 5 dB down at h7 and up at h3

variants.name: tank-3.6
variants.note: the organ's longer GS tank, on a voice that did not ask for it — the tank is host-wide, so this is what the organ's fix costs every other program

variants.name: tank-3.6
variants.note: the reference carries a 2 s hall the model cannot reach on the power-on tank

variants.name: hall
variants.note: the longer tank with the organ's own send pulled back, so the extra decay does not also arrive louder

variants.name: no-16
variants.note: the 16' rank all but silent — the registration question the three gated dimensions cannot settle

variants.name: perc-quiet
variants.note: half the shipped level: whether the ping sits under the registration or on top of it

variants.name: perc-loud
variants.note: the ping well forward, which is how a jazz registration is usually drawn

variants.name: drive-least
variants.note: the smallest drive that is not off, level-matched - the knob steps straight to tanh(x)/tanh(1), so this is the question of whether ANY amplifier belongs here

variants.name: drive-mild
variants.note: 1.5 dB of crest off a held chord, level-matched so loudness does not decide the choice

variants.name: drive-hard
variants.note: 2.9 dB of crest off, level-matched; the far end of what a rock organ's amplifier plausibly does

variants.name: di-fitted
variants.note: what a fit against the direct reference returns. It closes most of the gap it was aimed at - the voice sits 12 dB over that reference at 2 kHz rising to 40 at 6.35 - and it is a candidate rather than a fit because one product at the pickup can bound a voice and cannot target it: nothing here says whether this reference's darkness is the instrument or the library. These keys reach programs 26 and 27 only; the same fit on the amplified end is filed under p029, which is where it can be heard against a reference that carries a rig

variants.name: di-fitted-sustained
variants.note: the same reference fitted again with the decay bounded to what that reference measures: a median 5.91 dB/s over its own gate, so 10.2 s to 60 dB, against the 4.5 s the table states. It generalises - two held-out notes score 0.877 where the probe scores 0.893 - and it lands the whole-grid level within 0.6 dB of the reference where the shipped voice sits 5.0 dB under. It is a candidate rather than a fit because of what it costs the note's shape: rendered crest falls from 18.4 dB to 13.8 against the reference's own 20.6, which leaves the bound amplifier 2.7 dB of compression where the rig case asks for 3.0, and that gap is the pick transient rather than any knob here - none of the excitation knobs ends at a limit. Letting the decay run free instead reaches 36 s and 8.9 dB of crest, which inverts the rig relation outright

variants.name: amp-cleanCombo
variants.note: the same voice through the cleanCombo amplifier. The trim differs per amp only so the ten are comparable: levelDb sits after the amplifier, not before it, so it scales the output and changes nothing about the tone - measured identical crest at every value from 0 to 60 dB. What drives an amplifier here is `drive` alone

variants.name: di-fitted
variants.note: the direct fit carried onto the copy that voices this program, which is the measurement that says what it costs the amplified end. Against this program's own reference it improves rather than breaks it, at the shipped rig gain and over all 35 notes: brightness 43.60 to 25.27 per cent of the reference centroid, the partial stack 7.28 to 4.45 dB, body under the note 46.69 to 35.27, the double decay 10.43 to 5.56 dB/s, and the five rows whose decays were too far apart to compare all come back. Tone-to-noise is the one that does not follow, 7.80 to 8.25 dB out

variants.name: di-fitted-drive-0.75
variants.note: the same fit with the crunch rig driven harder, which is what a darker string in front of the same amplifier asks for. It centres brightness on the reference - the signed median goes to +3.21 per cent - and the per-note figure is the best in the sweep at 22.29. It is not free: the partial stack goes back out from 4.45 to 4.93 dB and tone-to-noise from 8.25 to 8.78, so the drive is buying a centre and selling scatter. Judge it against di-fitted by ear

variants.name: ring-2.3x
variants.note: a longer ring than the one now shipped, fitted to the first 0.25 s rather than to the 60 dB span the table was set from. The two references are not one envelope over two slots, which is what held this back: at the one note their grids share they agree on ring (0.66 against 0.68 s) and on centroid (443 against 440 Hz) and part company everywhere else - h2-h5 sit 25 to 60 dB apart and the attack is 20 ms against 5 - so a rosewood bar of either kind rings about the same at the same pitch and what separates the two instruments is spectrum and strike, both of which each patch voices on its own. One shared note is thin evidence for a library's provenance, so this is a candidate still and the ear still decides.

variants.name: ring-3.4x
variants.note: the same alternative on the xylophone: fitted to the first 0.25 s, where the shipped value comes off the 60 dB span. The two references are not one envelope over two slots, which is what held this back: at the one note their grids share they agree on ring (0.66 against 0.68 s) and on centroid (443 against 440 Hz) and part company everywhere else - h2-h5 sit 25 to 60 dB apart and the attack is 20 ms against 5 - so a rosewood bar of either kind rings about the same at the same pitch and what separates the two instruments is spectrum and strike, both of which each patch voices on its own. One shared note is thin evidence for a library's provenance, so this is a candidate still and the ear still decides.

variants.name: even-register
variants.note: the loop lowpass opened and the darkening moved to a patch filter that tracks the key. The reference's spectral tilt is the same at every note - -11.5 to -14.7 dB per octave of harmonic number over the whole compass - where the model runs -2.2 at the bottom to -18.1 at the top, because its only tone control is fixed in Hz. On the centroid the model goes from 4.12x the reference at the low probe note down to 0.67x at the high one, and this candidate brings that to 1.72x down to 0.99x. The cost is the reason it is a candidate: the model's only between-partial energy is the buzz's high-frequency spray, so darkening it deletes the noise as well as the tilt and tone-to-noise goes from 5 dB cleaner than the reference to 13

variants.name: flat-velocity
variants.note: velocity almost stops opening the excitation, which is what a fit returns and is not what a bachi does. It improves five readings - the level range from 7.9 to 3.7 dB too wide, the double decay from 73 to 58 dB/s short, tone-to-noise from 5.4 to 1.7, the held decay from 3.4 to 1.2 and the partial stack by a decibel - and takes the brightness median the other way, from 149 to 199 per cent. Judge it by ear against the plectrum, since the measurement cannot say whether a harder stroke should brighten this instrument

variants.name: keyed-filter
variants.note: the patch's own filter closed to 1.15x f0 and tracking the key, which no flute patch does today: h2-h6 goes from -19 to -38 dB and stays flat across the range for 1 dB of level. The reference sits at -70, so this is 20 of a 45 dB gap; every knob on the engine put together gives 7, and the four that give more than 3 collapse the level to a third because they are loop gain rather than timbre

variants.name: vibraslap-thinned
variants.note: the vibraslap's rattle thinned out - the one key in the kit whose decay length already matches while its crest sits 10.5 dB under both references, so what is wrong is the shape inside the envelope and not its length. A fit sparsens the collisions and pulls the plate back, which is the mechanism the residual pointed at, and takes crest from 5.1x the reference kits' spread to 2.3x, brightness from 1.5x to 0.6x, attack from 1.0x to 0.4x and level from 1.8x to 1.3x. The cost is the velocity range, which goes from 0.8x to 1.3x and is the only reading that leaves the spread: hear whether a harder strike should open this instrument that much before it lands

variants.name: scrapers-speak
variants.note: the cabasa, maracas, long guiro and both cuicas given a rise time. Their envelope attack is the shaker and scraper helpers' own 0.5 ms literal, shared by all nine members and never fitted against anything, where both reference kits agree these instruments take 11 to 30 ms to speak - the cabasa at 30.0 and 29.2. Each is set to a third above the nearer reference edge, which takes the five notes' attack from 7.8x the reference kits' spread to 2.4x and the whole kit's attack p90 from 24.9 ms to 19.2, with the level and the per-octave decay marginally better and nothing leaving the spread. Three of the nine are deliberately untouched: the short guiro already measures 20.0 ms against 20.5 because the collision density ramps it without the envelope, and the tambourine and vibraslap are inside. What this cannot settle is character - a 40 ms swell turns the cabasa's chk into a shh, and the references may be recording a player's gesture rather than the instrument

variants.name: crash2-and-china-reopened
variants.note: the second crash and the china cymbal given back a filter corner. Both carry one under 600 Hz - 368 and 515 Hz against 3.0 to 5.2 kHz on the five cymbals the same factory call builds - and both measure 22 to 31 dB dark in band tilt and 35 to 67 percent low in brightness, against a reference whose two crashes sit within 2 percent of each other in centroid. The corner cannot be moved on its own: on these two voices it is also the level, so opening it raises the note about 31 dB and the level fence charges more for that move than the corrected spectrum is worth, which is why a search over the corner alone walks it further shut. Fitted with the corner and the gain together, then the gain set to bring the level back to the reference, which every other term is blind to - at a fixed corner the whole term set is bit-identical across the gain axis. Crash 2 goes from 28-31 dB dark to within 2.5 dB, brightness from -63/-67 percent to -13/-18, band shape 19.1 to 11.5 and level -16.5/-6.5 dB to -2.1/+1.0; the china from 22-25 dB dark to within 6 dB, brightness from -35/-41 percent to within 5, band shape 19.1 to 9.6 and level -18.4/-13.1 dB to -2.0/+1.3. Held-out velocities generalise on both. Two residuals are untouched and are not this: the crash still speaks 48 ms early at the softest hits, and the china's per-octave decay stays 11 dB/s off there. What this cannot settle is whether a crash opened this far is the one the kit wants - it is a wash the shipped values had removed, so there is nothing to compare it against by ear until it is heard
